problems.problem: Unverifiable quote presented inside a high-confidence entry. The trans-sports entry (confidence: high) asserts that at the University of Arkansas in 2022 on the 'Educate Don't Mandate Tour' Kirk said such policies force women to live under 'the tyranny of men who think they're women'. I could not locate this quote, or a University of Arkansas stop, in any source. The 'Educate Don't Mandate' tour is real (CU Boulder, April 2022, documented by Colorado Times Recorder) but this specific line is not attested anywhere I could find.
problems.evidence: Targeted searches for the exact phrase 'tyranny of men who think they're women' returned zero attestations — only unrelated Kirk/trans material (transgendermap.com, Media Matters, factually.co). The Media Matters March 2022 piece documents him urging men to physically prevent trans athletes from competing, not this phrasing.

problems.problem: Paraphrases are placed in the `verbatim` field. For a persona whose whole point is not attributing invented statements, this is the highest-risk defect in the dossier. At least three Oxford Union 'verbatim' entries are reconstructions, one with an invented opening clause.
problems.evidence: Dossier verbatim: 'only one sex gets criticized and called toxic. Maybe that creates a backlash.' Actual transcript (singjupost.com): 'Only one chromosome set gets criticized, called that they're terrible and awful... Maybe that creates a backlash.' Dossier verbatim: 'Men in the West, we as men are here to be protectors and defenders and providers.' Actual: 'We as men are here to be protectors and defenders and providers.' — 'Men in the West,' is added. Dossier: 'We want to have the fertility rates reverse.' Actual: 'reversed.' Dossier: 'we wouldn't need as many third-world immigrants if we didn't kill our babies.' Actual: '...if we didn't kill our babies all the time in the womb.'

problems.problem: A real quote is anchored to a source that does not contain it. The higher-education entry gives verbatim 'These kids are going into debt to study things that don't matter to go find jobs that will not exist in five years' with source_url pointing at the Fox News 2022 'College Scam' book article. The Fox News piece exists (25 July 2022) but does not contain that line; the line is in the June/July 2025 YWLS podcast transcript.
problems.evidence: WebFetch of the Fox News URL confirmed the article exists and returned Kirk's actual quote there ('there must be an agreed upon consensus that higher education has become a scam') and explicitly reported the dossier's quoted sentence as NOT present. Fetch of podscripts.co returned it verbatim: 'these kids are going into debt to study things that don't matter to go find jobs that will not exist in five years'.

problems.problem: Both 'could NOT locate the original post' claims are wrong, and one of the two quotes is misworded as a result. The 2018 feminism post and the 2025 'feminism must be defeated' post are both locatable on X, and the 2025 one is misdated by about two and a half weeks.
problems.evidence: 'Feminism must be defeated for the west to be saved' — x.com/charliekirk11/status/1931091462546239693; the snowflake ID decodes to ~6 June 2025, not 'May 2025 (post-Oxford Union)'. The 2018 post — x.com/charliekirk11/status/1043558317208084480, ID decodes to 22 Sept 2018, and its text reads 'Feminism is much more about hating men than empowering women', not 'has become much more about'. The 'has become' wording and the tail 'For a culture to survive we need strong men and women—not strong women and weak men' appear only in the advocacy secondary sources (endtodv.org, dailydeclaration.org.au).

problems.problem: Material omission: the dossier's central framing ('his position is NOT women may not work'; position 10 as 'the libertarian escape hatch') omits documented Kirk positions that are considerably harder on sex roles in employment and on family law. A persona built only on the listed entries will be systematically softer than the record.
problems.evidence: Media Matters documents Kirk arguing men should not be allowed to be preschool teachers, and that '80 to 90 percent of all kindergarten, first, and second grade teachers are women and it should be that way' — a sex-typed-occupation claim absent from the dossier. Kirk also posted 'No-fault divorce and radical feminism are abominations' — a concrete policy position that cuts directly against the dossier's repeated claim that he 'offers almost no policy content'. Also absent: his stated opposition to women in frontline combat roles, and his Iced Coffee Hour (June 2025) line that women should find a husband before 25.

problems.problem: Factual error about Erika Kirk's age, used to score a rhetorical point.
problems.evidence: Dossier: 'his own wife Erika was 31 when they began dating.' Reporting on their meeting (August 2018) has Erika, born 1988, about to turn 30, with Kirk 24. The verifiable irony is the five-year age gap and his own late-20s marriage, not '31'.

problems.problem: Internal inconsistency in how one quote is rendered between the positions list and the rhetorical-moves list.
problems.evidence: Position 9 gives 'I don't know the solution as much' as an admitted quote; the rhetorical_moves section gives 'I'm not sure of the solution… we need to start being louder and louder about the problem.' The transcript supports the second: 'I'm not sure of the solution, but we need to start being louder.'

problems.problem: Unverified tail appended to a verified quote.
problems.evidence: The 2023 YWLS trans-athlete quote is attested as 'creepy, narcissistic freaks who think they are men wearing dresses to compete in sports' (Media Matters). The dossier appends 'against many of you', which I could not verify.

problems.problem: Some 'reasoning patterns' are the researcher's construction presented as description of Kirk, including one that supplies an argument the dossier itself concedes he never made.
problems.evidence: 'Nested-submission structure… male authority is conditional on male accountability. This is how he neutralises the abuse objection rhetorically' — the same entry then admits 'he generally does not address' the abuse objection. Similarly, 'he deliberately relocates the claim from religion to biology so that a secular opponent cannot dismiss it as sectarian' attributes intent with no source. By contrast the definitional demand, symmetry test, hardest-hypothetical answer, uncited number, and register-switching are all directly evidenced in the transcripts.

problems.problem: Unflagged tension inside the abortion entry: the stated position ('banned in all cases except a genuine threat to the mother's life') is undercut by the quote in its own source_desc.
problems.evidence: Same Snopes-verified Jubilee appearance: 'it is a growing consensus in the pro-life world that abortion is never medically necessary.' If abortion is never medically necessary, the life-of-the-mother exception does no work. The dossier presents the exception neutrally without noting he empties it.

corrected_recommendation:
The dossier is fundamentally sound and its central recommendation stands: the "Kirk said women may not work" reading is a verified strawman, and the YWLS transcript qualifiers ("You have the agency to do that", "It's not about prohibitive") are real. No fabricated quote was found. But the following must be amended before it is used to build a persona.

DROP OR DOWNGRADE:
1. Trans-sports entry (position 20): delete the University of Arkansas 2022 "tyranny of men who think they're women" clause entirely — unattested anywhere. Keep the Newsom and 2023 YWLS material, and trim the 2023 quote to the verified span, ending at "...to compete in sports" (drop "against many of you").

RE-ANCHOR:
2. Higher-education entry (position 8): move the verbatim "These kids are going into debt..." from the Fox News URL to podscripts.co (YWLS, June/July 2025). Fox News/The College Scam supports only the general "higher education has become a scam" claim.

CORRECT THE VERBATIM FIELDS (replace paraphrase with transcript text):
3. Position 4 → "Only one chromosome set gets criticized, called that they're terrible and awful… Maybe that creates a backlash."
4. Position 23 → "We as men are here to be protectors and defenders and providers." (delete "Men in the West,")
5. Position 24 → "We want to have the fertility rates reversed."
6. Position 16 → "In the UK and America we wouldn't need as many third world immigrants if we didn't kill our babies all the time in the womb."
7. Position 7 → "if you're gonna find your life partner, like that's actually a really good reason to go to college."
8. Position 9 source_desc → replace "I don't know the solution as much" with "I'm not sure of the solution, but we need to start being louder."

UPGRADE SOURCING (both "could not locate original" notes are wrong):
9. Position 1: original is x.com/charliekirk11/status/1043558317208084480, 22 Sept 2018, and reads "Feminism is much more about hating men than empowering women." Raise confidence to high, but mark the "has become much more" wording and the "strong men and women—not strong women and weak men" tail as advocacy-secondary variants, not the post text.
10. Position 2: original is x.com/charliekirk11/status/1931091462546239693, ~6 June 2025 (not May). Raise confidence to high and fix the date.

FIX:
11. Position 12: Erika was about to turn 30 (born 1988) when they met in August 2018, not 31; Kirk was 24. Reframe the irony as the five-year age gap.
12. Position 13: note that "abortion is never medically necessary," from the same appearance, functionally voids the life-of-the-mother exception the position statement grants him.

ADD (the persona will misrepresent him by omission otherwise):
13. Sex-typed occupations: he argued men should not be preschool teachers and that ~80–90% of early-grade teachers being women "should be that way." This materially qualifies the dossier's "not prohibitive / libertarian escape hatch" framing — his occupational views are not neutral about who does what work.
14. No-fault divorce: "No-fault divorce and radical feminism are abominations" (X). This contradicts the dossier's repeated claim that he offers "almost no policy content"; the counter is not only "which policy?" but "why is your only concrete policy restrictive rather than redistributive?"
15. Women in frontline combat: documented opposition, absent entirely.
16. The Iced Coffee Hour (June 2025) "find their husband before they're 25" — a sharper, better-sourced version of the deadline argument.

LABEL:
17. Mark the reasoning_pattern fields as the researcher's analytic reconstruction, not Kirk's own self-description — specifically the "nested submission / male accountability" and "relocates the claim from religion to biology" entries, which attribute intent and, in the first case, supply an argument the dossier concedes he never made. A persona that improvises from those will generate defenses Kirk never offered, which is the same failure mode as a strawman in the opposite direction.

The gaps section is honest and should be kept as-is, with one refinement: the "murky, middle gray area" clip can be narrowed to on-or-before 3 May 2025 (X post 1918527113818255751), though the venue remains unestablished — do not assert one.
surviving_claims: The YWLS 2025 podcast transcript (podscripts.co) is authentic and contains, verbatim: 'I hope that some of you guys walk away with a warning that a career-driven life is very empty'; 'the most miserable and depressed people in America are career-driven early 30-something women'; 'If you are single by the age of 30, you have a 50% chance of never having kids'; 'If they want to go work, fine. Okay, great. You have the agency to do that'; 'It's not about prohibitive'; 'it's actually reverse liberty'; 'the man needs to do everything imaginable that he possibly can'; 'if you use daycare I'm not judging you'; 'I'm not sure of the solution, but we need to start being louder'; and the 1985 37-weeks vs 56-weeks claim.

The central corrective claim survives: hostile summaries rendering Kirk as 'women should not work' clip out a qualifier he actually stated on the record. Freethought Now does characterize him as 'outright saying that women should not work', while his own released transcript of the same summit says the opposite in permission terms. The dossier's warning about this discrepancy is verified and important.

Media Matters, June 2023 YWLS, Grapevine TX: 'You're going to have to choose which one matters more' and 'there are a lot of successful, 35-year-old orthopedic surgeons that have cats, and not kids, and they're very miserable' — verified exactly, asked by a student pursuing orthopedic surgery.
Snopes verified the Jubilee 'Surrounded' exchange: 'Calm down, the answer is yes, the baby would be delivered', from 'Can 25 Liberal College Students Outsmart 1 Conservative?', September 2024.

Oxford Union, 20 May 2025 (singjupost transcript): 'we're actually living under a hyper feminist west that is toxic'; 'we learn about toxic masculinity from ages 8... We never talk about toxic femininity'; the third-world-immigrants line; the fertility-rates line; the Tinder/hookup line; and the Texas '200,000 new babies net over the last 18 months' claim.

Boise State 'Prove Me Wrong', 15 April 2025 (KTVB/Idaho Press): 'They're told that one in five women have sexual encounters that result in rape. We as men know that's a bunch of rubbish… we're tired being called rapists at every turn', plus 'pathologically insane'.

Newsom podcast, 6 March 2025: 'The young man who's about to win the state championship in the long jump in female sports, that shouldn't happen' is verbatim accurate (Kirk said long jump; the underlying California case was a triple jump).

Fox News 'Ingraham Angle', 8 September 2025: 'Young women who voted for Kamala Harris, they want careerism, consumerism and loneliness' — verified, paired with 'Trump voters, young men, they want family, children, and legacy'.

The birth-control and 'not at their prime' remarks are from a TPUSA Faith event at Fervent Church, Las Vegas, going viral 3-5 April 2024. The dossier's warning that 2025 recirculations misdate these to March 2025 is correct and is one of its most useful contributions.

The gender-pay-gap entry is correctly and honestly sourced: Kirk's 29 January 2018 speech clip and the TPUSA explainer, documented and rebutted by Matthew Boedy; the dossier correctly declines to supply a verbatim it could not obtain.
The HuffPost 'MRS degree' entry is accurate: a 14-year-old asked about political journalism at the June 2025 Dallas-area summit and Kirk pivoted to bringing back the MRS degree.

The gaps section is well-judged: the #MeToo gap, the Title IX gap, the 19th Amendment gap, the unsourced tombstone clip, and the post-death fabricated-quote warning are all confirmed as genuine unknowns or genuine risks. The Snopes standing collection '18 of Charlie Kirk's alleged quotes, investigated' exists and is the right verification backstop.

The identified 'seam' — 2018-19 equality-already-achieved framing versus 2023-25 careerism-is-the-problem framing — is real and both endpoints are independently documented (Jan 2018 wage-gap speech and June 2019 X post on one side; 2023-25 YWLS material on the other).
The register-switching observation is verified in both directions on video: fairness framing with Newsom, 'creepy, narcissistic freaks' at the 2023 YWLS.
Tilly Middlehurst is real and did debate Kirk at the Cambridge Union; the description of her pre-mapping his pivots is supported.
